description:
Mars has no GPS. So we're building one.

ARES (Astronaut Route & Exploration System) is an interactive Martian map that uses NASA data to plot routes that are safe and scientifically worth the trip. We're looking for coders, web devs, data analysts, UI/UX designers and planetary science nerds! No expert experience needed, just curiosity!
summary:
ARES is a human-centred Marswalk navigation and mission-planning system designed to help future astronauts explore the Martian surface more safely and effectively.

The platform combines NASA and USGS planetary data into one interactive interface where astronauts can explore Mars in 3D, select locations, save waypoints, compare FAST and SAFE routes, inspect terrain conditions, and understand the scientific context of their destination. SAFE routing considers elevation, slope, ascent, and distance rather than simply choosing the shortest path.

ARES also includes a guided mission mode built around Jezero Crater and Wildcat Ridge, which allows user to experience how the system could support a real surface exploration scenario. An integrated ARES AI assistant helps explain route decisions, terrain information, and mission context in plain language.

By bringing navigation, science, terrain awareness and mission information together at the scale of an individual Marswalk, ARES bridges the gap between global planetary mapping tools and the hyperlocal decisions astronauts will need to make on the surface of Mars.
details:
ARES is a browser-based Marswalk navigation and mission-planning system designed to support route planning and terrain awareness for future human exploration of the Martian surface.

The platform combines an interactive 3D Mars environment with location selection, waypoint management, route planning, terrain analysis, and EVA time estimation in a single web application. Users can explore the Martian surface, select locations, save waypoints, and define a starting point and destination for route calculation.

ARES provides two routing approaches: FAST and SAFE. FAST calculates a direct, distance-oriented route, while SAFE evaluates alternative nearby route corridors using available terrain information. The route assessment considers factors such as distance, elevation, slope, and total ascent. These approaches allow users to compare route characteristics rather than relying exclusively on distance.

The system uses Mars elevation data to assess terrain conditions along calculated routes. Its terrain analysis identifies slope variations and categorizes terrain segments into hazard levels. This provides additional information about potentially challenging sections of a planned Marswalk.

ARES also supports round-trip planning by calculating outbound and return journeys independently. It presents individual and combined route metrics, including total distance and estimated EVA duration. Users can compare the estimated mission duration against a configured EVA time limit to understand whether a planned journey fits within that time constraint.

The application includes a text-based AI assistant, ARES AI, powered by the Groq API. It allows users to ask questions in natural language and receive conversational responses about Marswalk navigation and related topics. The current assistant implementation is text-based and does not yet provide continuous access to live mission telemetry or the complete calculated mission context.

ARES is developed as a web application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Its interactive planetary environment uses the ArcGIS Maps SDK for JavaScript and Mars mapping and elevation services. The application is deployed through Vercel.

An important design consideration is the distinction between terrain measurements, calculated estimates, and safety conclusions. Route recommendations depend on the available elevation data and the system's implemented evaluation logic. In particular, the SAFE routing approach is a prototype decision-support method, not a guarantee of astronaut safety or a certified operational navigation system.

The objective of ARES is to demonstrate how planetary mapping, route computation, terrain assessment, round-trip planning, EVA time estimation, and conversational assistance can be brought together in a single interface for human-centered Mars exploration planning.
